solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Country shows a wild desire about pound, losing money

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter standing for money is dropped from what has been built
about says the first pieces wrap round the weight abbreviation

parts.note: a mania is a wild, obsessive desire
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Some nation is caught in a frenzy of craving for sterling while running out of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' here is the unit of weight, not sterling as the surface suggests; 'shows' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balkan state on the Adriatic coast, so a straightforward example of a country.

clue.text: Legal document left with section missing

indicators.note: missing says a stretch meaning section is absent from the longer word

parts.note: departed means left, gone away
a part is a section

explanation.surface: A legal paper has been handed over with one clause gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal signed instrument, such as one conveying property, is the classic legal document.

clue.text: Sport's function, mostly one encountered in football club

indicators.note: in places the shortened word and the numeral inside the club abbreviation
mostly means the word for function loses its final letter

parts.note: a role is a function
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sport's purpose seems to be described in terms of someone met at a soccer club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is a noun in the surface but here means fun or play; 'encountered' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sport in the old sense of merry play or fun matches a playful romp.

clue.text: Superficial SF film carried by Universal

indicators.note: carried by says the film title is held inside the word for universal

parts.note: cosmic means universal, relating to the whole universe
E.T. is Spielberg's famous science-fiction film

explanation.surface: A shallow science-fiction film distributed by Universal Studios.
explanation.walkthrough: Universal looks like the film studio but is just the adjective meaning of the whole cosmos.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cosmetic affects only the surface appearance, hence superficial.

clue.text: Brutally caned with canes in expression of power

indicators.note: brutally signals the letters of the two words are roughly knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Savage caning, with canes, as a demonstration of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendance is dominance or supremacy, the state in which power is exercised over others.

clue.text: One ball sent flying about for example

definitions.text: One ball sent flying about for example

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the abbreviation for example
sent flying means the letters are scattered into a fresh order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, and ball is taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket ball knocks a bail flying, as one instance of a dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket two bails sit on top of the stumps; the one on the batsman's leg side is the leg bail, which a ball can send flying.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes one of the bails, the leg-side one, being knocked off by a delivery.

clue.text: Student in time getting support for part of maths course

indicators.note: in says the learner letter sits within the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time
L is a learner, as on the L-plate
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A pupil is taking a long time to get help with part of a mathematics syllabus.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of mathematics using symbols for numbers is a core component of any maths syllabus.

clue.text: Party goers losing heart under supervision? It's a drag

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: losing heart means everything but the first and last letters of goers is dropped

parts.note: led means guided, so under supervision

explanation.surface: Partygoers lose their spirit under watchful eyes, finding the whole thing tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a drag' sounds like boredom but literally means something that is dragged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled pulled across snow by a dog team is literally dragged along, a witty reading of drag.

clue.text: Grandeur shown by gallery products on board

indicators.note: on, with board, means aboard a ship, so the other pieces go inside the vessel's abbreviation

parts.note: board stands for a ship here, given by SS, the steamship abbreviation
the Tate is a London art gallery
lines are ranges of products, as in a product line

explanation.surface: Magnificence is displayed by an art gallery's goods aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention: placed between S and S, the abbreviation for steamship. 'shown by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateliness is dignified, imposing magnificence, a close synonym of grandeur.

clue.text: Chap lasted out end of Stalinism? Not this poet

parts.note: a man is a chap

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their usual order
end of picks only the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man held out until Stalinism ended, but the poet did not survive.
explanation.walkthrough: Osip Mandelstam was persecuted for an epigram mocking Stalin and died in a labour camp, so he did not outlast Stalin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian poet Osip Mandelstam died in the Gulag, so he is the poet who did not see Stalinism end.

clue.text: River linking Kiel and Berlin?

indicators.note: linking points to the junction of the two city names, keeping only the letters on either side of where they meet

explanation.surface: A question about a German river joining the port of Kiel to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The join between the two city names, end of Kiel and start of Berlin, gives the river; the Kiel Canal does reach the Elbe estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: A major central European waterway flowing through Germany into the North Sea.

clue.text: Row about Government Act upset wild creature

indicators.note: about says the tier word wraps round the government abbreviation

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: upset means the letters of act are tipped into another order

explanation.surface: A dispute over some piece of legislation riles a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger cat is a small striped wild feline such as the margay or oncilla, a wild creature.

clue.text: Heart breaking, friend runs off — disaster?

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of heart are broken up and reassembled
off says the runs letter goes away from the friend word

parts.note: a Quaker is a member of the Religious Society of Friends
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Heartbreak as a friend walks out: is it a catastrophe?
explanation.walkthrough: The capital-less 'friend' hides Friend, a Quaker; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent tremor of the ground is a natural catastrophe, one example of a disaster.

clue.text: News item, mostly substantial, had an effect

indicators.note: mostly means the word for substantial loses its last letter

parts.note: tidy means substantial, as in a tidy sum
bit means took hold or had an effect, as when brakes bite

explanation.surface: A news story, largely weighty, made an impact.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel of gossip or interesting information, the American spelling of titbit, is a small piece of news.

clue.text: Not very clear argument finally leads to tirade about poor clues

indicators.note: finally takes just the last letter of argument
about says the rant word goes round the scrambled clue letters

parts.note: a rant is a tirade

indicators.note: poor signals the letters of clues are badly arranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder as printed lacks the N the answer needs

explanation.surface: A muddled argument ends with a rant about badly written crossword clues.
explanation.walkthrough: T, then RANT around SLUCE, the anagram of CLUES signalled by 'poor', gives TRANSLUCET: one N short. 'leads to' is a link. The setter's slip; the definition is solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Translucent material lets light through but blurs images, so it is less than fully transparent.

clue.text: Note riders heading off invaders as before

indicators.note: heading off means the word for riders loses its first letter

parts.note: horsemen are riders

explanation.surface: A memo says cavalry are off heading off invaders, just as in earlier times.
explanation.definitionFit: Vikings from Scandinavia raided and invaded Britain in medieval times, so they are invaders of old.

clue.text: Person from Pacific island capable of handstand?

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing on its head means read bottom to top, so the word must read the same either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An islander from the Pacific who can do a handstand.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a palindrome, so this down entry upside down still reads the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny island republic in the central Pacific, and its people are named after it.

clue.text: Some colours send a scene soaring — here's impact of blues

indicators.note: soaring in a down entry means the letters rise, read from bottom to top
some says only part of these words is used, a run of consecutive letters

explanation.surface: A painting's colours make a scene take flight, showing the effect of blue pigment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here's' is a link. Blues here means low spirits, not the colour the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the blues means feeling low, and the effect of that is sorrow or melancholy.

clue.text: Increasingly prepared to chance some meat

definitions.meaning: more reckless, more willing to take risks: the comparative of rash
a slice of bacon is a portion of meat

explanation.surface: Someone growing bolder about gambling on a bit of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the comparative of a reckless adjective; the other is a thin cut of bacon or ham.

clue.text: Baron? No Baron left — title returned

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: returned means the word for title is sent back, read right to left

parts.note: a name is a title

explanation.surface: A puzzled cry about a peer who departed, his title given back.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Baron as one example of the defined class.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is the lowest rank of the peerage, one example of a titled aristocrat.

clue.text: A Bishop brought in gift for another primate

indicators.note: brought in says the article and the bishop letter go inside the word for gift

parts.note: a boon is a gift or blessing
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop delivered as a present for a fellow archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop, or rather an archbishop, is a primate in the church sense; hence 'another' primate, the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This large African monkey belongs to the primate order, a different sort of primate from a churchman.

clue.text: Foreign words helping you to fulfil your duty

indicators.note: the language fills out the phrase, its letters sitting inside your duty

explanation.surface: Phrases in another language that help you carry out your obligations.
explanation.definitionFit: The national language of Pakistan, spoken also in India, is foreign speech to an English solver.

clue.text: Town's sober nature disturbed without right

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of sober nature are stirred up, with the right letter taken away

explanation.surface: A town whose staid character has been upset, minus anything right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without right' removes one R from the letters of SOBER NATURE before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside resort in East Sussex, famously genteel, is an example of an English town.

clue.text: Busy with University's indication of further reading?

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
PTO, please turn over, printed at the foot of a page tells you to read on

explanation.surface: A university's guidance on what to read next.
explanation.definitionFit: Being occupied with something, as in what are you doing now, is an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: New article produced with intense yellow cloth

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
keen means intense, as a keen wind

explanation.surface: A fresh item made of vivid yellow fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a buff-yellow cotton fabric originally made in Nanjing, so a yellow cloth.

clue.text: Chap's receiving excessive onset of heat? Not so much, it seems

indicators.note: receiving says the word for chap's takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: his means belonging to a chap
OTT is over the top, excessive

indicators.note: onset of takes only the first letter of heat

explanation.surface: A man is getting an excessive start of fever; or perhaps not quite so much.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays off 'heat' just before it: not so much heat, merely a little warm.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish softens an adjective, so a fairly warm state is somewhat less than fully hot.
